summary: Operators can change their Firebase Auth login email and password directly from Settings → Security on web Wasm, desktop JVM, and Android. Email change uses verifyBeforeUpdateEmail (sends a confirmation link to the new address; the email only flips after the operator confirms, so no fake "changed" state). Password change reauthenticates with the current password first, then sets the new one, surfacing auth/requires-recent-login and auth/wrong-password errors loudly. Every successful credential mutation writes an activity_log audit entry. No Cloud Function is added; this is client-side Firebase Auth on all three platforms.

backend.plan: NO Cloud Function. All writes are client-side Firebase Auth on each platform. WEB commonMain AuthClient.kt: add to the facade (after :26) suspend fun updateLoginEmail(currentPassword: String, newEmail: String): AuthOpResult = platformUpdateEmail(currentPassword, newEmail) and suspend fun updatePassword(currentPassword: String, newPassword: String): AuthOpResult = platformUpdatePassword(currentPassword, newPassword); add a sealed AuthOpResult { object Ok; data class Failure(code) with a friendly map covering auth/requires-recent-login -> 'Please sign in again to change this.', auth/wrong-password & auth/invalid-credential -> 'Current password is incorrect.', auth/email-already-in-use, auth/invalid-email, auth/weak-password -> 'Choose a stronger password (6+ chars).', auth/too-many-requests, auth/network-request-failed }; declare new expect funcs platformUpdateEmail/platformUpdatePassword alongside :50-55. NOTE: use verifyBeforeUpdateEmail (NOT the deprecated updateEmail) so the new address must be confirmed; the facade returns Ok meaning 'verification link sent', and the UI copy must say so (do not claim the email already changed). WEB wasmJs: in firebase-bridge.js extend the firebase-auth.js import (:8-11) to add EmailAuthProvider, reauthenticateWithCredential, updatePassword, verifyBeforeUpdateEmail; add two __fb methods inside the frozen object (before :448): updateLoginEmail:(currentPassword,newEmail,cb)=> { const u=auth.currentUser; if(!u){cb(JSON.stringify({ok:false,error:'auth/no-current-user'}));return;} reauthenticateWithCredential(u, EmailAuthProvider.credential(u.email,currentPassword)).then(()=>verifyBeforeUpdateEmail(u,newEmail)).then(()=>cb(JSON.stringify({ok:true}))).catch(e=>cb(JSON.stringify({ok:false,error:e.code||String(e)}))); } and updatePassword:(currentPassword,newPassword,cb)=> same reauth then updatePassword(u,newPassword). Add matching @JsFun externals + suspendCancellableCoroutine actuals in AuthInterop.wasmJs.kt mirroring platformSignIn (:43-59), parsing {ok,error} into AuthOpResult. WEB jvm: in AuthInterop.jvm.kt FirebaseRestAuth add suspend fun updateEmail/updatePassword. REST flow uses the Identity Toolkit accounts:update (setAccountInfo) endpoint with the current idToken. For password: POST $IDENTITY:update {idToken, password:newPassword, returnSecureToken:true}; reauth-equivalence is enforced by first re-running signInWithPassword(email, currentPassword) to prove the current password (fail with auth/wrong-password mapped via existing mapError :205-219 if INVALID_PASSWORD) and to mint a fresh idToken (satisfies requires-recent-login), then call :update; on success swap the stored idToken/refreshToken/expiresAtMillis from the response. For email: Identity Toolkit has no verifyBeforeUpdateEmail REST that sends a confirm link to the NEW address without changing it immediately; to keep parity with the web 'verify-before-update' contract and avoid a silent immediate swap, send accounts:sendOobCode with requestType=VERIFY_AND_CHANGE_EMAIL, {idToken, email:'<current>', newEmail:'<new>'} after the signInWithPassword reauth; return Ok = 'verification link sent'. Expose new internal actuals platformUpdateEmail/platformUpdatePassword delegating to FirebaseRestAuth, mirroring :233-241. ANDROID AuntieRepository.kt: add suspend fun updateLoginEmail(currentPassword, newEmail): Result<Unit> = runCatching { val u=auth.currentUser ?: error('Not signed in'); u.reauthenticate(EmailAuthProvider.getCredential(u.email!!, currentPassword)).await(); u.verifyBeforeUpdateEmail(newEmail.trim()).await() } and suspend fun updatePassword(currentPassword, newPassword): Result<Unit> = runCatching { reauthenticate as above; u.updatePassword(newPassword).await() }, each .onFailure { AuntieLog.e(...) }. import com.google.firebase.auth.EmailAuthProvider. After each success call repository.logActivity(ActivityLogEntry(actionType='AUTH_EMAIL_CHANGE_REQUESTED' / 'AUTH_PASSWORD_CHANGED', ...)). On web wire AuditLog.fire(scope, client, actorId=authUser.uid, actionType, description) at the SecurityPanel call sites after Ok.

errorHandling: Fail loud on every platform, never fake success. Web: AuthOpResult.Failure.friendly maps auth/requires-recent-login, auth/wrong-password, auth/invalid-credential, auth/email-already-in-use, auth/invalid-email, auth/weak-password, auth/too-many-requests, auth/network-request-failed to human strings; surfaced via the existing StatusToast (ToastKind.Error) in SecurityPanel. The email flow uses verifyBeforeUpdateEmail, so the success toast explicitly says the change is pending confirmation (no false 'email changed' claim). jvm: REST errors mapped through the existing mapError (AuthInterop.jvm.kt:205-219); a failed reauth signInWithPassword returns auth/wrong-password; network exceptions return auth/network-request-failed; token-refresh failures already fail closed (:139-176). risks: 1) verifyBeforeUpdateEmail vs updateEmail: modern Firebase forbids the immediate updateEmail when email-enumeration protection is on; must use verifyBeforeUpdateEmail on web+android, and on jvm REST use VERIFY_AND_CHANGE_EMAIL oob (not accounts:update email) so behavior matches — otherwise the desktop would silently change the email immediately, breaking parity and the 'pending confirmation' contract. 2) jvm has no native reauthenticate; re-running signInWithPassword is the equivalence — confirm the Identity Toolkit :update accepts the freshly minted idToken (it does) and that minting it satisfies the password-change recency requirement. 3) After a successful password change the jvm session's idToken/refreshToken are rotated by :update; must re-store them or subsequent Firestore REST calls 401. 4) After verifyBeforeUpdateEmail the local authUser.email is stale until the operator confirms and the next onAuthStateChanged/token refresh fires; UI copy must not imply the email already changed. 5) The shared Firebase web appId is technically an Android app id (firebase-bridge.js:18-19); ensure the Auth provider settings allow these operations for this app. 6) Android verifyBeforeUpdateEmail needs an ActionCodeSettings/authorized-domain for the continue URL; default (null) is fine but confirm the auth domain auntieos-ttpc.firebaseapp.com is authorized. 7) Rebaseline visual goldens deliberately (per MEMORY: re-baseline only with --no-build-cache and verify the live artifact, since BUILD SUCCESSFUL can ship stale wasm).
